head.title: bluedoc site: tandem demo films, Plans first
head.subtitle: Replace the single-page clips' hero role with terminal-plus-bluedoc films that show the whole loop, starting with a Plans hook aimed at AI engineers.
head.tldr: Record 30-second **films**: the agent's terminal on the left, the bluedoc page on the right, both live. A viewer sees the plan open, the reader pick and approve, and the agent receive the answers and start coding. The first film is the **Plans hook**: it opens on the wall-of-text pain and ends on *your agent was already waiting*. 9 steps cover a two-window stage in the recorder, the hook, more films, the clips 1.0.7–1.0.14 made stale, and the site. **9 questions** need a pick, each with a recommendation.

sections.title: Context
sections.lead: Today's 100 clips each show one browser tab, were recorded on bluedoc 1.0.2–1.0.6, and never show the agent's side.

sections.title: Approach
sections.lead: A stage page puts a scripted terminal beside an iframe of the real bluedoc server; the existing CDP recorder films it as one take.

sections.title: Steps
sections.lead: 9 steps: recorder support first, then the hook, then more films, the clip refresh and the site.

sections.title: Open questions
sections.lead: Pick one option per question; my recommendation is starred. Your picks go with **Approve plan** or **Request changes**.

sections.title: Risks
sections.lead: The main risk is a film that looks staged; the real server output is the guard.

sections.title: Verification
sections.lead: Done when the hook matches the beat sheet, reads at 1024 px, and the site builds.

items.md: A 5–8 s loop of one bluedoc page at 1280 × 800, one feature per clip. `public/clips/<name>.{mp4,webm,poster.webp}`, recorded by `npm run clips`.
A 20–32 s loop of a **stage**: a terminal window and a bluedoc browser window side by side, both driven live, telling one task from prompt to payoff.
A recorder-only HTML page that lays out the two windows; the bluedoc window is an iframe of the real local server.

rows: `clips/run.mjs:19` fixes `VIEW` at 1280 × 800; `recorder.mjs` `encode()` hardcodes width 1280; one tab per take (`followNewTab` only switches tabs).
A film needs a wider frame and two windows in one take.
No clip shows a terminal. The agent's half of the loop (the gate opening the page, `serve.py wait` returning) is invisible.
The difference from Anthropic's `html-plan` skill and Plannotator is that the agent waits and reads the answers itself; only the terminal shows that.
Decision rows and reply boxes changed in 1.0.7, 1.0.8 and 1.0.10; drawings keep a pin since 1.0.13.
`every-option-rows`, `every-accept`, `every-more`, `every-item-comment`, `every-conversation`, `every-draw`, `every-marks` and the `plan-*` clips show the old UI.
No clip for attachments (1.0.9), video in screens (1.0.14), pinned and stale evidence, or Approve blocked while an item asks for more details.

steps.label: The scenario opens the stage with the plan doc's URL.
It types the prompt and prints the agent's tool lines.

serve.py wait returns; its stdout is printed as-is.

6ce47f40c0bc8460.caption: Plans hook, beat sheet (about 32 s, loops). Terminal strings in quotes are the real hook.py and serve.py output, captured in the take.
rows: *Without bluedoc*: a 120-line plan scrolls past, ending on Claude Code's “Would you like to proceed? 1. Yes … 3. No, keep planning”.
Window absent; the terminal fills the frame.
Cut. Fresh session, `⏸ plan mode on`. Typed: `Let shoppers save a cart and come back to it later.`
`● Read(web/src/cart/cartStorage.ts)` · `● Write(docs/plans/saved-carts.bluedoc.json)` · `● ExitPlanMode` ⎿ “bluedoc opened this plan for the reader at … The reader answers on that page, not here.”
The saved-carts plan opens at its TL;DR.
`● Bash(serve.py wait … --kind any)` running in the background; spinner.
Scrolls to Approach: the new parts drawn amber and dashed.
**Accept recommended** stars every question at once; then the reader also ticks *Guests, by email link*, and pins *Run it on the existing jobs queue* on the sweeper step.
**Approve plan** → the dialog lists the picks and the comment → Approve → chip **Approved · rev 1**.
“--- bluedoc approval (reply …, rev 1, …) ---”, `# Plan approved: Acme Shop: saved carts (rev 1)`, `## Decisions` with each pick, the note, “--- end ---”.

`● ExitPlanMode` ⎿ “Approved in bluedoc, rev 1 … Implement that rev of the doc, with the reader's decisions and notes from the approval.” · `● Write(…/0012_saved_carts.sql)`; ghost input *also add an undo for restore*.

items.title: Make the frame size and encode width per scenario
items.md: `VIEW` in `clips/run.mjs` and the width in `encode()` come from the scenario (`export const view = {width, height}`), default 1280 × 800; films use 1600 × 1000 at dpr 2. `Clip.astro` takes `width`/`height` props for its poster and video and drops the fake browser bar for films.

items.title: Add the tandem stage and its terminal pane
items.md: `clips/stage/tandem.html` lays out the terminal window (about 34 % wide) and a bluedoc window with an iframe of the doc URL. `terminal.js` renders a terminal look (prompt box, `●` tool lines with `⎿` results, a spinner with a seconds counter, the plan-mode footer) and exposes `term.type`, `term.print`, `term.tool`, `term.spin`. `clips/lib/stage.mjs` serves the stage and gives scenarios `c.term`.

items.title: Let the actor click and wait inside the iframe
items.md: Localhost ports are same-site, so the iframe stays in the stage's process. `chrome.mjs` records the iframe's execution context from `Runtime.executionContextCreated`; `actor.mjs` resolves selectors and `ev`/`waitFor` there and offsets pointer coordinates by the iframe's box.

items.title: Drive the agent side from the real server
items.md: The scenario runs the real `serve.py open` and a background `serve.py wait --kind any`, and prints wait's stdout into the terminal when it returns, so the approval frame on screen is the real one. Only typing speed and the spinner are scripted; the gate's text is copied from `hook.py` `instructions()` at record time, not retyped.

items.title: Record the Plans hook and cut it to the beat sheet
items.md: Takes until the contact sheet matches the beat sheet: prompt typed by 7 s, page open by 10 s, approval frame readable for at least 4 s. Captions are drawn by the stage, not burned in afterwards.

items.text: How do we build a film?
items.sub: Recommend a recorded stage: one shareable MP4 with the real page and real terminal output.

choices.label: Recorded stage
choices.md: One take of a stage page with the terminal beside the real page. One file works on the site, X and LinkedIn; terminal text is pixels, so the terminal font is sized for a 1024 px wide player.

choices.label: HTML terminal + video
choices.md: devicemcp.ai's Agents section: the terminal is live HTML synced to a browser-only video by a timing table. Crisp and editable text, but nothing to post on social, and a timing table to keep in sync on every re-record.

choices.label: Real screen recording
choices.md: Record a real Claude Code session and browser on a desktop. Most authentic, but not reproducible by `npm run clips`, and personal paths leak (devicemcp's hero shows one).

items.text: Which agent does the hero film show?
items.sub: Recommend Claude Code: the plan-mode debate is happening there.

choices.label: Claude Code
choices.md: Plan mode plus the ExitPlanMode gate; the HN *Plan mode is dead* thread is about it. Shown as a terminal look with the name, no Anthropic logo or mascot.

choices.label: Codex
choices.md: `/plan` with the Stop-hook gate; its users ask for exactly this in codex#19125. A smaller audience for the first film.

choices.label: Claude Code and Codex
choices.md: Two takes of the same story with a switch above the player, like devicemcp's device switch. About double the hero work.

items.text: How does the plan reach the page in the hero?
items.sub: Recommend plan mode: it shows the gate, which no competitor has.

choices.label: Plan mode gate
choices.md: Shift+Tab, the agent writes the bluedoc plan and calls ExitPlanMode; the hook opens the page and tells the agent to wait. Shows that bluedoc plugs into the flow they already use.

choices.label: /bluedoc-plan command
choices.md: The user types `/bluedoc-plan …`. Simpler to read, but looks like one more tool to remember.

items.text: Does the hero open on the pain?
items.sub: Recommend a labelled 3 s before beat: name the pain, then answer it.

choices.label: 3 s before beat
choices.md: *Without bluedoc*: a plan wall ending on *Yes / No, keep planning*, captioned *Approve this wall of text?*. Costs 3 s of a 32 s loop; labelled, so it isn't passed off as bluedoc's output.

choices.label: Straight into the flow
choices.md: Starts on the prompt. Shorter, but the viewer has to supply the pain themselves.

choices.label: A separate before/after film
choices.md: A full film of the copy-paste loop next to the bluedoc loop. Strongest contrast, one more film to make.

items.text: What text sits on the film?
items.sub: Recommend three short captions drawn by the stage.

choices.label: Three short captions
choices.md: *Approve this wall of text?* · *Or answer it.* · *Your agent was already waiting.* Readable muted and on a phone.

choices.label: None
choices.md: devicemcp.ai's choice. Cleaner, but assumes the viewer reads Claude Code output fluently.

choices.label: Step subtitles
choices.md: A caption per beat. Most explicit; busier, and the captions compete with the terminal text.

items.text: Which line does the hero end on?
items.sub: Recommend *Your agent was already waiting*: it names what html-plan and Plannotator don't do.

choices.label: Already waiting
choices.md: *Your agent was already waiting.* Lands on the terminal receiving the answers; the no-copy-paste difference without naming anyone.

choices.label: No copy, no paste
choices.md: *No copy. No paste. Your agent's listening.* States the difference outright; longer, and *listening* is softer than what the terminal shows.

choices.label: Stop approving walls
choices.md: *Stop approving walls of text.* Reuses the pain line; better as the opener than as the payoff.

items.text: Which films do we make after the hook?
items.sub: Recommend Send it back and Review: the two loops a plan reader hits next.

choices.label: Send it back
choices.md: Request changes → rev 2 with the change marked → approve. Answers *if you say no the plan disappears*.

choices.label: Review
choices.md: Findings pinned to diff lines, decided one by one, fixed by the agent. Reaches the code-review crowd.

choices.label: Questions
choices.md: Four clarifying answers on one page instead of a timing-out picker.

choices.label: Design
choices.md: Pins on a mockup, the agent revises, onion-skin compare. The most visual; the least about terminal pain.

items.text: Where does the hero film play?
items.sub: Recommend the Atlas variant: its big product frame was built for this.

choices.label: Atlas variant
choices.md: Replaces the plan-tour clip in `/variants/atlas/`. No change to bluedoc.ai's home until you choose a design.

choices.label: Current home
choices.md: Goes into the live home hero now. Ships the film sooner; the current hero has no big frame, so it needs a new row.

choices.label: Both
choices.md: Both pages get it; the most work now.

items.detail: The live home stays as it is until you pick between the current design and the Atlas variant.

items.sub: Recommend yes: the film is the launch post.

choices.label: 16:9 and 1:1 cuts
choices.md: Two more encodes of the same take (1920 × 1080 and 1080 × 1080) for X and LinkedIn, with the captions kept inside the safe area.

choices.label: Site only
choices.md: One 16:10 file; social posts reuse it letterboxed.

rows: Print the real `serve.py wait` stdout and the gate text taken from `hook.py`; only typing speed and the spinner are scripted.
Terminal text unreadable in the site player
Terminal font at least 15 CSS px at 1600 wide; check the poster at a 1024 px player and on a 390 px phone.
Same-site iframe, so one process; if contexts misbehave, attach with `Target.setAutoAttach` (flatten) instead.
Name it, mimic the text layout only; no Anthropic logo or mascot.
Films go stale again at 1.0.15 (edit gate)
The films show no edit gate; re-record the hook once 1.0.15 changes what the terminal prints.
Unverified quotes end up on screen
Captions use only phrasing from GitHub and HN; the Reddit and X items stay out until checked in a browser.
CRF tuned per film, WebM alongside, `preload="none"`, poster at the payoff; target ≤ 6 MB MP4 for 32 s.
